items.title: Section: Four More Reasons for Silence, Closing the Teaching Gateway

items.zh: 應知復有四種因緣，如來宣說不可記事。謂諸外道妄宣說故，不如理故，引無義故，唯是諍論所依處故。有二因緣能引無義。一者、遠離思因果故；二者、遠離思染淨故。云何遠離二邊？
items.en: One should know there are four further causes for which the Tathāgata declared certain matters unanswerable: that non-Buddhist teachers falsely proclaim answers to them, that they do not accord with reality, that they bring no benefit, and that they serve only as grounds for contention. Two causes explain why they bring no benefit: drawing attention away from reflecting correctly on cause and effect, and drawing attention away from reflecting correctly on defilement and purity. What is avoiding the two extremes?

items.title: Section: Six Extremes to Avoid, and Six Things Never Worth Speculating About

items.zh: 當知略有六種。謂遠離增益非實有邊、遠離損減真實有邊、遠離妄執常邊、遠離妄執斷邊、遠離受用欲樂邊、遠離受用自苦邊。如是應知，如前處處已廣分別。云何不可思議？當知略有六種不可思議。謂我思議、有情思議、世間思議、有情業果思議、諸修靜慮靜慮境界、諸佛世尊諸佛境界。
items.en: One should know there are, briefly, six kinds: avoiding the extreme of exaggerating what is not truly existent into existence, avoiding the extreme of diminishing what is truly existent into non-existence, avoiding the mistaken clinging to eternalism, avoiding the mistaken clinging to nihilism, avoiding indulgence in sensory pleasure, and avoiding self-mortification. What is the inconceivable? One should know there are, briefly, six kinds of the inconceivable: speculation about the self, about sentient beings, about the world, about beings' own karmic fruit, about the absorption states of meditators, and about the Buddhas' own domain.

items.zh: 此中我思議、有情思議、世間思議，或依見思議，或不依見思議。

items.title: Section: Sixteen Ways the Mind Spins Stories About a Self That Isn't There

items.zh: 我思議者，謂如有一，依止身見，如是思議：我於過去為曾有耶？為復無耶？於三世中乃至廣說。又復思議我是有色，後當有想、後當無想、後當非有想非無想。如我有色，我無色亦爾。若廣宣說，如梵網經。如常見論者，如是斷見論者、現法涅槃見論者，當知亦爾。計前際邊、計後際邊，如其所應皆當了知。又復思議命即是身、命異身異，又此我我遍一切處、無二無別、無有缺減。
items.en: Speculation about the self is as when one, relying on the view of a real self, speculates: did I exist in the past, or did I not, and so on across the three times, extensively explained. One further speculates whether the self possesses form and, in the future, will have perception, will lack perception, or neither, and the same applies to a formless self. One further speculates whether the life-principle is identical to the body, or different from the body, or whether this self, at once a form-self and a formless self, pervades everywhere, without division and without lack.

items.title: Section: Where Do Beings Come From — A Question Better Left Alone

items.zh: 有情思議者，謂如有一，即依身見，如是思議：今此有情從何而生？是諸有情誰之所作？乃至有情當何所往？是諸有情何處滅盡？
items.en: Speculation about sentient beings is as when one, relying on the view of a real self, speculates: from where do these beings arise? Who has made these beings? And where will these beings eventually go, and where will they finally cease?

items.title: Section: Āryadeva's Own Calm Before an Assassin, and Why a Buddha's Domain Cannot Be Guessed

items.zh: 世間思議者，謂如有一，即依身見，如是思議：世間是常，乃至廣說。或依法性，如是思議：此我法性、有情法性、世間法性從何而生？不能唯依法爾道理。是故說此名為思議不思議處。有情業果思議者，由四種相不可思議。謂處所差別故、事差別故、因差別故、異熟果差別故。諸修靜慮靜慮境界，由三種相不可思議。謂真如甚深義故、自在轉故、無漏界證得故。諸佛世尊諸佛境界，由五種相不可思議。即由如先所說三相。復由二相。謂無障故、成立有情所作事故。
items.en: Speculation about the world is as when one, relying on the view of a real self, speculates whether the world is permanent, and so on. Speculation about beings' own karmic fruit is inconceivable through four marks: differences of place, differences of bodily existence, differences of cause, and differences of ripened fruit. The absorption states of meditators are inconceivable through three marks: suchness's own profound meaning, freedom once mastery is reached, and the attainment of the undefiled realm. The Buddhas' own domain is inconceivable through five marks: the same three already stated, together with two further marks, being unobstructed, and accomplishing whatever task beings actually need.

items.title: Section: Sixteen Intentions Behind Everything the Buddha Ever Said

items.zh: 復次，當知意趣略有十六。謂示現意趣、乖離意趣、勸導意趣、讚勵意趣、慶喜意趣、令入意趣、斷疑意趣、成熟意趣、等持意趣、解脫意趣、別義相應意趣、諸能證者發生無罪歡喜意趣、諸能聽者於說者所發生尊重意趣、法眼恒轉意趣、多修諸善意趣、摧伏諸相意趣。云何
items.en: Furthermore, one should know that intention is, briefly, of sixteen kinds: the intention to show, to inspire aversion, to exhort, to praise and encourage, to rejoice, to bring in, to cut off doubt, to bring to maturity, concerning concentration, concerning liberation, of special meaning, to produce faultless joy in those who realise it, to produce respect in listeners towards the teacher, that the Dharma eye continually turns, to cultivate abundant wholesome conduct, and to subdue every clung-to characteristic.

items.title: Section: All Dharmas Without Self-Nature — The Intentions Come to Their Close

items.zh: 真義理門，由遠離二邊理門
items.en: The intention to subdue every clung-to characteristic is as the World-Honoured One declared: all phenomena are without self-nature, without arising and without ceasing, originally still, their own nature already nirvana. This is the intention to subdue every characteristic. The above has broadly discerned true meaning, realisation, teaching, avoiding the two extremes, the inconceivable, and intention, the six distinct gateways of reasoning embracing the noble teaching's own meaning.

items.title: Section: Four Foundations of Mindfulness Answer Four Ancient Errors

items.zh: 謂於安立所有苦諦乃至道諦，略有四種妄增益邊。一、我增益邊，二、常增益邊，三、淨增益邊，四、樂增益邊。如此即是四種顛倒，為對治彼，說四念住及四定智。由此因緣，所有我見皆是妄執我增益邊。
items.en: Regarding the established truths of suffering through the path, there are, briefly, four kinds of false exaggeration: the exaggeration of self, of permanence, of purity, and of pleasure. These are the four inversions; to counter them, the four foundations of mindfulness and the four kinds of settled wisdom are taught. Because of this, every view of a self is simply the false exaggeration of self.

items.zh: 廣說應知如前有尋有伺地。由彼廣辯執有我者不應理故。又若略說，離彼諸蘊，生故、相故及業用故，別有我性不可得故。又異彼相安住諸行所有我性，當知畢竟定無所有。又彼常性不應道理，當知如前已廣分別。又有六種不淨性，如聲聞地已廣顯示。又有三種苦性，如有尋有伺地已廣顯示。損減邊者，謂即於彼諸聖諦中，隨所安立諸諦相狀，執為無性、顯為無性。何以故？

blocks.text: Why some questions are better left alone, and the many hidden intentions behind the Buddha's words.
False proclamation, not according with reality, no benefit, and grounds only for contention. Master Cháng Bǎi: the first is moving away from reflecting on cause and effect, which hinders practice.
Master Cháng Bǎi: to hold that all things are real is exaggeration; that all are utterly non-existent, diminishment.
Holding the self to be the body, or different from it, or both. Master Cháng Bǎi explains each form.

The domain of meditators differs in place, event, cause, and ripened fruit. A buddha's domain has the same three marks, plus two: it is unobstructed, and accomplishes whatever task is needed. Master Cháng Bǎi: beings are born at times as humans, ants, animals, or gods; the differences are in their own bodies.
Master Cháng Bǎi: an intention is a further purpose, an overtone within the words that guides beings elsewhere.
The four inversions are countered by the four foundations of mindfulness.
"An overtone within the words." Reading the Buddha's teaching well means listening for what it is trying to do, not only what it says.

quiz.q: What are the four causes for which the Tathāgata declared matters unanswerable?
options: the Buddha does not know, disciples are too dull, time is short, and words fail
avoiding thought of cause, purity, pleasure, and permanence
differences of place, event, cause, and fruit
others falsely proclaim them, they accord not with reality, bring no benefit, and only ground contention
quiz.why: The treatise lists false proclamation by others, not according with reality, bringing no benefit, and serving only as grounds for contention. The two causes of no benefit are explained just afterwards.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain the first cause of bringing no benefit?
options: moving away from good friends and losing all guidance
moving away from reflecting on defilement and purity
moving away from the community to dwell alone
moving away from reflecting on cause and effect, hindering practice
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the first is moving away from reflecting on the principle of cause and effect, failing to accord with it, which hinders practice and brings no benefit. Reflecting on defilement and purity is the second.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi state the difference between exaggeration and diminishment in a line?
options: holding all things truly real is exaggeration; holding all things utterly nonexistent is diminishment
praising the Dharma is exaggeration and criticising it diminishment, so that whatever says it is good or bad falls to one side
practising much is one; practising little the other
greed is one; hatred the other
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: to hold that all things are real is exaggeration; to hold that all things are utterly nonexistent is diminishment. Both of these extremes must be avoided, as the first two of the treatise's six say.

quiz.q: Through which four marks is beings' karmic fruit inconceivable?
options: differences of place, of event, of cause, and of ripened fruit
suchness, mastery, the undefiled realm, and non-obstruction
past, present, future, and all three together
wholesome, unwholesome, neutral, and pure
quiz.why: The treatise lists differences of place, event, cause, and ripened fruit. Suchness and the rest are the three marks of meditators' states, and these with two others make the five of the Buddhas' domain.

quiz.q: Which two marks does the Buddhas' domain add to those of meditators' states?
options: mastery and the undefiled realm, since meditators' states have only suchness
being unobstructed, and accomplishing whatever task beings need
suchness's profound meaning, and the undefiled realm
differences of place, and of ripened fruit
quiz.why: The treatise says the Buddhas' domain has the same three marks stated before, with two further: being unobstructed, and accomplishing whatever task beings actually need. Mastery and the undefiled realm are already among the three.

quiz.q: What does Master Cháng Bǎi say intention means?
options: simply the literal sense, each of the Buddha's sentences having a single meaning read straight
the Buddha's moods and preferences
the interests of the audience
a further purpose, an overtone, a meaning within the words that leads elsewhere
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: intention is a further purpose, commonly called an overtone, a meaning within the words that guides beings elsewhere. The lecture gives two sets of readings for the sixteen, so only this general sense is tested.

quiz.q: This is rendered "whether this self pervades everywhere." What is lost?
options: nothing: the repeated 我 is a copying slip with one self meant, so deleting it is right
the two 我 are a form self and a formless self, both held as self; the English merges them
遍 is lost
命 is lost
quiz.why: The life-principle being the body holds self as form, and being different holds it as formless; the repeated word holds both as self. Master Cháng Bǎi explains the first of these, and the English single self loses the layered view.

quiz.q: The mark 事差別 is rendered "differences of event." Why is this off?
options: nothing: 事 means the happenings of life, such as promotion or loss
事 means the bodies beings obtain, such as human, ant, or god, not events
it should be differences of place
it should be differences of time
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: one is at times born as a human, an ant, an animal, or a god, these being differences in beings' own bodies. The difference concerns the body obtained, and the word event misleads the reader.

quiz.q: What does the treatise teach to counter the four exaggerations?
options: these are four wrong views, and the four immeasurables and means of gathering are taught
these are four afflictions, and four right efforts are taught
these are four sufferings, and the four truths are taught
these are the four inversions, and the four foundations of mindfulness and four settled wisdoms are taught
quiz.why: The treatise says these are the four inversions, and the four foundations of mindfulness and four settled wisdoms are taught against them. The lecture gives two readings of the wisdoms, so their definition is not tested.
